g3ela-31-1-teach-morph: [curious] What happens when you add a part to a word? Replay. Re is a prefix at the front. It means again. Replay means play again. Painless. Less is a suffix at the end. It means without. Painless means without pain. Every part on this page is one you already know. Read the parts, tap See what was hiding, then type the missing part of each word.
g3ela-31-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Daring. Here's my sentence. Grace made a daring trip across the stormy sea. One, read the sentence: she went, even though it was dangerous. Two, look for word parts: dare, plus i n g. Three, check it. Daring means brave enough to take a risk. Now fill in each sentence from the word bank, and play the matching game.
g3ela-31-1-teach-gram: [warmly] A whole year of rules, in one sentence. when grace saw the wreck she telled her father. When starts the sentence: capital W. Grace is a name: capital G. A comma goes after wreck, to close the opening part. And telled should be told. Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap all six words in the passage that need fixing.
g3ela-31-1-teach-spell: Front or back? Replay: the part re is at the front, so it's a prefix. Painless: the part less is at the end, so it's a suffix. Think about the questions, and tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words: prefix at the front, or suffix at the end.
g3ela-31-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Unsafe. Find the prefix: un. It means not. So unsafe means not safe. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-31-2-teach-vocab: Here's a good-character word that isn't in the game. Loyal. A loyal friend sticks by you, even when things get hard. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.
g3ela-31-2-teach-gram: Simple, compound or complex? Grace rowed, and her father helped. Two complete thoughts joined by and: compound. Although the sea was rough, they rowed on. Although starts a part that can't stand alone: complex. Name each sentence, and tap Now check your thinking. Then tap the four words that are wrong.
g3ela-31-2-teach-spell: Clap it with me. Wonderful. Won, der, ful. Three beats, so I'd tap it. Brave? Just one beat, so no tap. Read the rule. Then tap every word in the sentences with three or more beats.
g3ela-31-2-teach-rwm: Let's try all three parts with a different sentence from Text 2. Mira's heart hammered. Part one, read like a reader. Mira is very scared. Part two, read like a writer. The author never says scared. She shows it with the body: a heart that hammers like a hammer on wood. Part three, write your own. My turn: Sam's hands shook on the rope. Now it's your turn with the author's sentence. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-31-3-teach-morph: Snap the parts together. Re. Paint. Repaint! To paint it again. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-31-3-teach-vocab: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Nobody was watching, but Leo gave back the extra change. That shows blank. Courageous? Hmm, not quite. Integrity? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.
g3ela-31-3-teach-gram: Be the editor. the boats oars were heavy and grace was tired. The gets a capital. Boat's gets an apostrophe: the oars belong to the boat. A comma goes before and. Grace is a name. Read the before and after, and tap Check yourself. Then fix the sentence in the gray box.
g3ela-31-3-teach-spell: Build it one beat at a time. Ev. Er. Y. One. Everyone! Four beats, in order. A chunk in the wrong place won't stick. Now tap the chunks in order to build each word.
g3ela-31-4-teach-morph: Quick question: what does un mean? Not! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Unbroken. Not broken. The boat came home unbroken. Say what the word part means. Then tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.
g3ela-31-4-teach-vocab: Watch me use a word about a book from this year. Integrity. Lucy showed integrity: she kept telling the truth about Narnia, even when nobody believed her. Now choose your word, and write your own sentence about a book.
g3ela-31-4-teach-gram: Two passes, like an editor. the keepers daughter was brave and she rowed hard. Pass one, capitals: The. Pass two, apostrophes and commas: keeper's, and a comma before and. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.
g3ela-31-4-teach-spell: Dice roll: lifeboat! Life, boat. Two beats. Tap Roll the dice, say the word, count its beats and say where they split. Then tap Check my answer.
